scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cante dolido que solo se canta en Semana Santa, al paso de las imágenes, a palo seco o con cornetas y tambores, por martinetes, siguiriyas (las más comunes), soleares, cañas o polos, con coplas de exaltación religiosa que exigen gran potencia de voz. Nace a finales del XIX en Cádiz: Enrique el Mellizo y sus hijos detenían al Nazareno desde los cuatro balcones de su casa con sus saetas. A él se atribuye la saeta por siguiriyas, que desarrolló Manuel Centeno en el siglo XX. Manuel Torre, el Niño Gloria, la Niña de los Peines, Manolo Caracol y Antonio Mairena eran esperados en Semana Santa para cantarlas sin amplificación desde un balcón a la altura de las imágenes; Manuel Mairena grabó un vía crucis entero. Un equipo francés grabó en directo a los saeteros de Jerez, Arcos y Lebrija en la Semana Santa de 1993 para la colección Flamenco vivo.

scenes.name: Demófilo y los Machado
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Antonio Machado y Álvarez, Demófilo, fue el primer autor español que dedicó un libro entero al flamenco: la Colección de cantes flamencos recogidos y anotados (1881), piedra angular de la flamencología moderna; escribió también sobre las saetas y dirigió la revista El Folclore Andaluz (1882-1883). Sus hijos, los poetas Antonio y Manuel Machado (autor de Cante hondo), heredaron la afición, y sus coplas se cantan a menudo sin que los cantaores sepan que son versos cultos. Calixto Sánchez dedicó a Antonio Machado un disco en 2001, y José Menese hizo suyas las letras de Francisco Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: La farruca y el garrotín
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes aflamencados de fuera de Andalucía. La farruca, gallega, llegó a Cádiz con los comerciantes gallegos del XIX y es más baile que cante; la popularizó Manuel Torre a principios del XX y hoy casi solo la canta Pepe Menese, con una letra de Moreno Galván que se hizo himno en la Transición. Su baile, viril, lo creó Faíco; Carmen Amaya lo bailó vestida de hombre, Falla lo incluyó en El sombrero de tres picos y la versión de Antonio Gades en la película de Los Tarantos, la última de Carmen Amaya, se enseña hoy en las academias. El garrotín viene del folclore asturiano y lo hicieron suyo los gitanos de Lleida; lo difundieron Carmen Amaya y la Niña de los Peines, que lo cantaba con aire de tangos, Faíco hizo sus coreografías y Blas Vega recogió una copla antigua cantada por el Chaparro en la Magna antología del cante flamenco.

scenes.name: Los fandangos de Huelva
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Huelva reclama la cuna del fandango andaluz y es la provincia con más estilos: las antologías recogen más de treinta y cinco, locales (Encinasola, el Alosno, Cabezas Rubias, Calañas, el Andévalo, Valverde del Camino) y personales, creados por profesionales como Paco Isidro, Pepe Rebollo, el Comía, Antonio Rengel, Pérez de Guzmán y Paco Toronjo; de fuera dejaron su sello el Gloria, Macandé, el Carbonerillo y Manolo Caracol. Paco Toronjo, fijo en los festivales desde finales de los sesenta y en las bienales de Sevilla, les dio una jondura difícil de imitar. El baile, de pareja y galanteo, se ve ya poco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Levante o de las minas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacidos del trabajo en las minas del siglo XIX en las sierras de Cartagena y La Unión y en Linares, La Carolina y Andújar: cantes de dolor profundo sobre la mina, sus accidentes y los compañeros muertos, hechos con fandangos regionales, murcianas, malagueñas y el cante de madrugá de los mineros. La taranta, el más significativo, tiene dos estilos, el de Linares (Gabriel Moreno, Carmen Linares) y el de La Unión (Encarnación Fernández, Pepe Cros), y Camarón le puso dulzura; el taranto, almeriense, tiene compás porque nació para el baile de Carmen Amaya en los cuarenta, con el Ciego de la Playa y Pedro el Morato. La cartagenera, de temas más urbanos, la fijó Antonio Chacón a finales del XIX y la cantaron Cayetano Muriel, Manuel Centeno, Manuel Torre y la Niña de los Peines. La minera se atribuye a Rojo el Alpargatero, Antonio Grau Mora, que hacia 1885 abrió en La Unión una posada que acabó en café cantante y oía cantar a los mineros de madrugada: es el gran creador de los cantes mineros. Las granaínas, de Frasquito Yerbabuena y sobre todo Chacón, son un cante casi barroco hoy cargado de vibratos operísticos. Sin minas, los concursos de Linares y La Unión mantienen vivos estos cantes.

scenes.name: Las cantiñas: alegrías, caracoles, mirabrás y romeras
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Mainstream Breakthrough in 1991
facts.body: Alternative rock had existed in a parallel universe for at least 15 years, but in 1991, the barrier collapsed, and it flooded into the mainstream. This shift was so significant that by the end of the year, alternative rock effectively ceased to be alternative, becoming the mainstream. "But in 1991, the barrier between the two rock universes collapsed. And alternative rock flooded into the mainstream."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Alternative Rock

facts.title: Grammy Award Category Introduction (1991)
facts.body: The "Alternative Album" category was first introduced at the Grammy Awards in 1991, years after alternative albums began to gain prominence. This marked a significant moment of formal recognition for the genre by the Recording Academy. "It wasn't until 1991 that the genre had its own category."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts
facts.name: Alternative Rock

facts.title: Impact on Music Industry (1991)
facts.body: Nirvana's *Nevermind* arrived when rock was stagnant, characterized by an "overabundance of classic rock acts" and "hair metal bands that had stopped being amusing with their stupid power ballads," alongside "crappy phony pop stars like vanilla ice and millie-vinyl." The album acted as a spokesperson for angry and scared Generation Xers during a recession and the Gulf War, leading to alternative music becoming mainstream and turning the rock world "literally upside down." "After Nevermind, what was once alternative became the mainstream."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Move to DGC Records (1991)
facts.body: Facing financial constraints from Subpop despite high hopes for the band, Nirvana signed a contract with DGC on January 4, 1991. Their decision was influenced by Sonic Youth's earlier move to the same label, with Kurt Cobain believing if it was good enough for Sonic Youth, it was good enough for Nirvana. "So on January 4th, 1991, it was announced that Nirvana had signed a contract with DGC. Now why DGC? Well, like Thurston Moore said, it was because Sonic Youth had chosen that company as their major label home."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: "Nevermind" Release Date (September 24, 1991)
facts.body: Nirvana's landmark album "Nevermind" was released on the exact same day as the Red Hot Chili Peppers' "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," September 24, 1991. "Same day as Nirvana's Nevermind."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

facts.title: Rain's Transformation into Oasis (1991)
facts.body: In 1991, after a gig by Liam Gallagher's band Rain, Liam and his bandmates asked Noel Gallagher to manage them. Noel refused to manage but offered to join as lead guitarist, stating his original songs were far superior to Rain's material, leading to the band accepting him and transforming into Oasis. "The band accepted, and that's when Rain started the Metamorphosis into Oasis."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Noel Gallagher Joins Rain, Band Becomes Oasis (1991)
facts.body: After a gig by Liam's band Rain in 1991, Liam and his bandmates asked Noel to manage them. Noel declined the management offer but instead proposed joining as their lead guitarist, citing his years of songwriting and the superior quality of his material compared to Rain's songs. The band accepted, initiating the transformation of Rain into Oasis. "The van accepted, and that's when Rain started the Metamorphosis into Oasis."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Reinvention in Berlin (1991)
facts.body: Facing the challenge of following up "The Joshua Tree," U2 struggled with early recording sessions for "Achtung Baby." Their relocation to Berlin, coinciding with the fall of the Berlin Wall, sparked a creative breakthrough as they embraced new influences like electronic, industrial, dance, and alternative music, leading to a deliberate reinvention of their sound and image. "But after moving to Berlin at around the same time the Berlin wall was coming down, things began to click."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Pre-Mainstream Status During Singles Filming (1991)
facts.body: During the filming of *Singles* in early 1991, the Seattle grunge scene was "basically unknown to people outside the extreme Pacific Northwest." Major label signings for bands like Soundgarden hadn't yet registered broadly, and key bands like Pearl Jam and Nirvana were still in their nascent stages, highlighting the scene's pre-explosion status. "At the time, the Seattle Gren scene was basically unknown to people outside the extreme Pacific Northwest."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: The Holy Trinity of Albums (1991)
facts.body: The "holy trinity of grunge albums" comprises Pearl Jam's "Ten," Nirvana's "Nevermind," and Soundgarden's "Badmotorfinger," all released in 1991. These three records provided a diverse selection of new guitar rock for listeners and were instrumental in launching grunge into the mainstream. "this record became the first of the holy trinity of grunge albums. It's 10 from Pearl Jeff."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Late 1991 Emergence and Teenage Engagement
facts.body: Grunge "hit in late 1991" and was a defining genre for teenagers, who "sucked up" music from bands like Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Alice in Chains, and Soundgarden during their formative years. This period was crucial for their musical identity formation.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: MTV Genesis (1991)
facts.body: The music video for Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" in 1991 is widely recognized as the video that ushered in the entire Grunge era. Its raw, energetic visuals, filmed in a high school gymnasium with real fans destroying the set, became an iconic representation of the genre. "And who could forget the video that ushered in the whole Grunge era in 1991?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 1

facts.title: Move to Warner Brothers (1991)
facts.body: The Red Hot Chili Peppers signed a new record deal with Warner Brothers, moving from EMI, which coincided with their recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik." "They had a new record deal, moving from EMI to Warner Brothers."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Collaboration with Rick Rubin (1991)
facts.body: Rick Rubin produced the Red Hot Chili Peppers' "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" album, bringing a new dynamic to their sound. "They had a new producer in Rick Rubin."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" Recording Location (April 1991)
facts.body: For the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," the Red Hot Chili Peppers moved into a historic mansion at 351 Laurel Canyon Boulevard, built in 1918. The house, with a reputation for being haunted and allegedly having secret tunnels to the nearby "Houdini Estate," was chosen by producer Rick Rubin for its isolated vibe. A Canadian company converted the basement into a recording studio. Chad Smith, however, was too unnerved by the house's atmosphere to stay there during sessions. "In April 1991, the Chili Peppers moved into a historic mansion at 351 Laurel Canyon, Boulevard that was built in 1918."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: Tour Openers for "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" Tour (1991-1992)
facts.body: During the tour supporting "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," the Red Hot Chili Peppers were joined by two emerging bands as their openers: The Smashing Pumpkins and Pearl Jam, indicating the significant cultural impact and growing status of the Chili Peppers. "One was called The Smash and Pumpkins, and the other was Pearl Jam."

facts.title: Hiatus for College (1991)
facts.body: In 1991, "On a Friday" entered an extended hiatus as all five members pursued higher education at different universities. Ed O'Brien went to Manchester University, Colin Greenwood studied English literature at Cambridge, Phil Selway also studied English literature at Liverpool University, and Johnny Greenwood enrolled in both music and psychology programs at Oxford. Tom York decided to take a year off before attending university. "In 1997, a 1991 on a Friday went on an extended sort of hiatus."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Post-Graduation Concerts (1991)
facts.body: The band's first concert after their graduation period took place on July 22, 1991, at the Hollywood in Oxford. Despite having played together "off and on for years" and estimated "at least 100 times" before, this gig was described as relatively modest: "five friends, two strobe lights and a smoke machine." A subsequent gig in October at the Jericho Tavern, known for hosting other Oxford bands like Supergrass, Ride, and Slowdive, proved to be a turning point. "The big day that everybody remembers is July 22, 1991. Just when they played a show at the Hollywood in Oxford, their first post-graduation concert."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Manic Hedgehog Tape (1991)
facts.body: This was a five-song cassette that "On a Friday" sold for three pounds at the local indie record store, Manic Hedgehog, where Colin Greenwood worked. Colin strategically "slipped a copy of this cassette" to any record label representatives who visited the store. This grassroots promotion led to an unprecedented 25 record company reps attending their pivotal gig at the Jericho Tavern. "That cassette ended up being referred to as appropriately the Manic Hedgehog tape and it featured songs like this. It's called Philip a Chicken."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Record Deal with EMI (1991)
facts.body: By the end of 1991, "On a Friday" was actively pursued by various record companies, culminating in a six-album deal with EMI, signed on December 21, 1991. This deal marked a significant milestone, although it came with a stipulation for the band to change its name. "On December 21, 1991, they signed an album deal with EMI."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Name Change to Radiohead (1991)
facts.body: After signing with EMI, the label expressed dissatisfaction with the name "On a Friday" and instructed the band to find a new one. Various suggestions were considered, including "Jude the Obscure" (deemed "too obscure" from the Thomas Hardy novel), "Music" (liked by Tom but rejected), and "Gravitates" (which "didn't have the right ring to it"). The definitive name, "Radiohead," was discovered when someone retrieved a 1986 Talking Heads album, "True Stories," from Tom York's DJ collection, which featured a song of the same name. The name change officially occurred at the end of 1991. "And so it came to pass that at the end of 1991, on a Friday, became known as Radiohead."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Heroin Addiction Begins (1991)
facts.body: Dave Gahan's heroin addiction began around 1991 after he moved to Los Angeles and became involved with the Jane's Addiction social circle, living a rock and roll lifestyle with his wife, Teresa. A wedding gift they received for their wedding was a lump of black tar heroin. "Heroin was Dave's thing, starting in about 1991."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.body: After their initial meeting and an exchange of gifts (a heart-shaped box from Courtney), Kurt and Courtney reconnected on May 29, 1991, at a Butthole Surfers show in Los Angeles, one month after Nirvana secured their major record deal. facts.title: "Killer Whale Tank" Story (May 1991)
facts.body: The most famous extended live version of "New Orleans is Sinking" features the "Killer Whale Tank" story, recorded at the Roxy in Los Angeles in May 1991. This recording was a highly sought-after bonus track on the "long time running" single, which was initially distributed exclusively to radio stations and not made available for public sale. "The most famous of all the extended live versions of New Orleans's sinking is the one with the Killer Whale Tank story. It was recorded at the Roxy in Los Angeles in May of 1991. And for years fans long to get their hands on this recording, but it was completely unavailable. And that's because it was only available as a bonus track on the long time running single. And this single was only distributed to radio stations. It wasn't designed to be sold to the public."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

And this single was only distributed to radio stations. It wasn't designed to be sold to the public."

facts.title: Formation and Early Days (1991)
facts.body: During the filming of *Singles* in early 1991, Pearl Jam had "barely been born." Eddie Vedder had recently moved from San Diego to Seattle and was "hanging out with his future bandmates," indicating they were in the very nascent stages of their formation, predating the grunge explosion. "As Singles started filling, Pearl Jam had barely been born, although Eddie Vetter had already moved from San Diego to Seattle where he was hanging out with his future bandmates."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: The Day of Jeremy Dell's Suicide (January 8, 1991)
facts.body: On the morning of Tuesday, January 8, 1991, Jeremy Dell woke at 7:10 AM, called a friend, Nancy, and mentioned he was already high from smoking weed, appearing happy. He arrived at Richardson High at 8:20 AM and gave other students a letter to be mailed, stating he wouldn't be around after school. After missing his 9 AM class, he arrived late to his second-period English class at 9:35 AM. When teacher Fay Barnette followed procedure to send him to the principal's office for a late slip, Jeremy instead went to his locker (number 540), retrieved the stolen .357 Magnum, returned to the classroom, placed his hall pass on the teacher's desk, and, turning to her, stated, "Miss, I got what I really went for." He then put the gun in his mouth and pulled the trigger in front of approximately 30 classmates, with the bang heard throughout the school. "He then got out the gun, put it in his mouth, and pulled the trigger. There were about 30 other kids in the room at the time."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Cultural Storm Timeline (1991-1997)
facts.body: Britpop is described as a "perfect cultural storm" that ran from about 1991 to 1997, following a six-year cycle including a build-up, a frenzy peak (12-18 months), and a long, slow decline. During this era, "London was swinging again" and British acts sold "tens of millions of albums." "This party ran from about 1991 to 1997."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Initial Lack of Soundgarden Recognition (1991)
facts.body: In early 1991, during the filming of *Singles*, Soundgarden's *Louder Than Love* album, despite being on a major label, did not register significantly "outside the metal community." This indicates that even within heavy music subgenres, the broader appeal of what would become grunge was still limited. "Yes, Soundgarden had signed to a major label and had released their louder than love album, but outside the metal community, it didn't really register."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Complex Family Life (1991-2015)
facts.body: Sinead had four children with four different men and married only one of them. She divorced her first husband, John Reynolds (father of Jake), in 1991. She had a daughter, Róisín, with Irish journalist John Waters in 1995, leading to a long and contentious custody battle. Her son Shane was born in 2004 with musician Donal Lunny, which created a scandal due to Lunny being married at the time. Her fourth child, Jeshua, was born in 2006 with Frank Bonadio. She also experienced three miscarriages and one abortion, later becoming a grandmother in 2015 at age 49. "Family life, though, was complicated. Shenade had four children with four different men, only one of whom she married."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Multiple Marriages (1991-2012)
facts.body: After divorcing John Reynolds in 1991, Sinead O'Connor married British journalist Nick Sommerlad in 2004, a union that lasted less than a year. She married musician and longtime collaborator Steve Cooney in 2010, also for less than a year. Her fourth marriage was a Las Vegas wedding to Irish psychotherapist Barry Herridge in 2012, reportedly lasting only a few weeks. "Her third marriage was in 2010 to Steve Cuny, a longtime friend and musical collaborator who played in her band."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Lollapalooza Performance (1991)
facts.body: Nine Inch Nails was an up-and-coming band featured on the bill for the first Lollapalooza tour, which aimed to bring the UK festival experience to America and fill arenas with alternative acts. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nine Inch Nails

facts.title: Alternative Rule (1991-1995)
facts.body: From mid-1991 through the end of 1995, alternative rock, fueled by grunge at its core and sustained by various other genres, dominated the music scene. This era introduced Generation X to a wide array of subgenres, paralleling the "endless" supply of fresh bands during the New Wave era. "And for the next five years, Alt Rock ruled, spread by the ideals of Lola Palusa and fueled by Grunge at its core and sustained by all kinds of other music."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Alt-rock

facts.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
facts.body: Nine Inch Nails, described as a "weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere," was part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which ultimately proved the significant demand for diverse, non-mainstream bands. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nine Inch Nails

facts.title: "White Man's Soul Music" (1991)
facts.body: Chris Christofferson described country music in 1991 as "white man's soul music," focusing on themes of drinking, cheating, and sex as subjects not typically found in pop music. This perspective, however, is considered problematic for implicitly excluding black performers and fans. "country is white man's soul music."

facts.title: Initiating Contact with Kurt Cobain (1991)
facts.body: After their initial meeting in 1989, Courtney Love, a friend of Jennifer Finch (L7) and former girlfriend of Dave Grohl, learned through Dave that Kurt Cobain reciprocated her interest. She then sent Kurt a distinctive package containing seashells, pine cones, miniature teacups, and a doll, all presented in a heart-shaped box. "And one day Courtney told Dave that she liked Kurt and Dave told Courtney that Kurt kind of liked her. That's when she gave Dave a package to give to Kurt."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: Courtney Love

facts.title: Developing Relationship with Kurt Cobain (1991)
facts.body: Courtney Love and Kurt Cobain "hooked up again" on May 29, 1991, at a Butthole Surfers show in Los Angeles, shortly after Nirvana signed their major deal. Their reunion was characterized by "instant attraction," escalating quickly from Courtney punching Kurt to wrestling and kicking, followed by sharing drugs such as Vicodin and high-powered cough syrup, resulting in them becoming "pretty much inseparable." "On May 29th, 1991, one month after Nirvana signed their major deal, Kurt and Courtney hooked up again at a butthole surfer show in Los Angeles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

facts.title: Peak Era (1991-1995)
facts.body: The period between 1991 and 1995 was considered the speaker's favorite era of music, as every day brought a new sound, song, or scene, indicating a rapid and exciting evolution of alternative music. "And it was, it was, it was a wild ride between 91 and 95 was my favorite era of music because every day you come into work and there'd be this new sound, this new song, this new scene that we never heard of."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: OGHONM 1000th Episode: The Q&A From the Live Recording
facts.name: Alternative

facts.title: Growth and Diversity (1991-1995)
facts.body: The period between 1991 and 1995 was described as a "wild ride" for alternative music, with new sounds, songs, and scenes emerging daily. This era encompassed grunge, American indie, the Lollapalooza generation, gangster rap, and the early stages of Britpop, showcasing immense musical diversity. "it was a wild ride between 91 and 95 was my favorite era of music because every day you come into work and there'd be this new sound, this new song, this new scene that we never heard of."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 1000th Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Alternative

facts.title: Inspiration from The Mansion – Blood Sugar Sex Magik Recording (1991)
facts.body: During the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" in a historic mansion, John Frusciante embraced the isolated and reputedly haunted environment. Unlike Chad Smith, who refused to stay there, Frusciante loved the house and found it inspirational, ready to disconnect from the outside world. He believed friendly ghosts resided there and even mused that the spirit of a person who died in the house might have influenced his guitar sound. "There are definitely ghosts in this house, said John, but they are very friendly."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1
facts.name: John Frusciante

facts.title: Aversion to Success and Depression (1991-1992)
facts.body: As "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" grew in popularity, John Frusciante became increasingly unhappy with the band's massive commercial success. He yearned for the underground scene, preferring small clubs over arenas, and his personality shifted from "manic, happy-go-lucky fun" to a more serious and depressed state. This created tension with the band, particularly Anthony Kiedis. He found a kindred spirit in Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who shared his desire for underground credibility, which further fueled his discontent with the Chili Peppers' mainstream success. "He wanted to be in a cool underground band. The success was way too serious for him."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1
facts.name: John Frusciante

facts.title: Innuendo (1991) - Graphic Complexity
facts.body: "Innuendo" is arguably the most graphically and iconographically interesting point in Queen's entire career due to its complex visual language. The music video for the title track is a highly intricate collage of various elements, including film footage, animation, and old recordings, all perfectly synchronized with the music, faithfully reflecting the song's complexity. "Si el Inuendo musicalmente es complejo, visualmente también es muy complejo."

facts.body: "Innuendo" is arguably the most graphically and iconographically interesting point in Queen's entire career due to its complex visual language. The music video for the title track is a highly intricate collage of various elements, including film footage, animation, and old recordings, all perfectly synchronized with the music, faithfully reflecting the song's complexity. facts.title: Hotel Suite Renamed and Renovated (1991, Recently)
facts.body: In 1991, the Queen Elizabeth Hotel received permission from Yoko Ono to begin renting room 1742 in John Lennon's name. More recently, all four rooms (1738, 1740, 1742, and 1744) where the couple stayed were combined into one large suite, featuring two bedrooms, a dining room, two lounges, two bathrooms, a pantry, and virtual reality goggles to experience the view from Lennon's perspective. Today, this renovated suite is known as the "John Lennon and Yoko Ono suite." "Years later, in 1991, the Hotel received permission from Yoko Ono to begin renting room 1742 in Lenin's name."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Last Ever Tour (1991)
facts.body: The multi-act bill of the first Lollapalooza in 1991 was put together by singer Perry Farrell specifically to support what was intended to be Jane's Addiction's last ever tour. "the singer for Jane's edition put together a multi-act bill to support what would be the last ever tour for Jane's edition."

facts.title: Founding Lollapalooza (1991)
facts.body: Perry Farrell, the singer for Jane's Addiction, conceived and established Lollapalooza in 1991, an "all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show" that famously featured a mix of alternative rock and hardcore rap bands. This festival was groundbreaking in bridging racial and social barriers through music. "In 1991, Jane's edition singer Perry Farrell came up with the idea of an all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show he called Lola Palusa."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Jane’s Addiction

facts.title: Lollapalooza (1991) Headliner
facts.body: Jane's Addiction headlined the very first Lollapalooza show, which began outside Phoenix on July 18, 1991. The festival was originally conceived as their farewell tour. "The lineup featured Jane's addiction, Susie in the bandsheets, living color, nine inch nails, butthole, surfers, raw on-span, iced tea and body count, and fishbone."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Jane’s Addiction

facts.title: Farewell Tour and Lollapalooza (1991)
facts.body: Jane's Addiction initiated the first Lollapalooza tour, with Perry Farrell using it as a vehicle to commemorate the band's farewell tour. They retired for the first time in August 1991, after the tour's final show in Hawaii. "The fact that Perry needed some kind of hope to commemorate Jane's Addiction's Farewell tour also helped."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Jane’s Addiction

facts.title: First Retirement (August 1991)
facts.body: Jane's Addiction retired for the first time in August 1991, concluding with the last Lollapalooza tour date on August 28th in Hawaii. "Jane's Addiction, they retired for the first time in August of 1991"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Jane’s Addiction

facts.title: Original Lineup's Last Show (1991)
facts.body: After the 1991 Lollapalooza tour, the band played a couple of contractual shows in Australia and Hawaii, with the very last show of the original lineup taking place on September 26, 1991, at the Aloha Tower in Honolulu. "The date I have for the very last show is September the 26th, 1991 at the Aloha Tower in Honolulu."

facts.title: Early Days (1991)
facts.body: During the filming of *Singles* in early 1991, Alice in Chains was still in its early stages, primarily "trying to be a glimy hair metal band." This indicates their musical evolution was ongoing and predated their full embrace of the grunge sound that would later define them and the Seattle scene. "Allison James was still trying to be a glimy hair metal band."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Escalating Addiction and Financial Loss (Post-1991)
facts.body: As Alice in Chains gained popularity, Layne Staley's increased wealth fueled his intensifying drug habit, which reached a tipping point after 1991. By the mid-90s, his condition was very poor. His addiction caused Alice in Chains to lose substantial income because they couldn't be booked for tours, including bailing as the opener for a Metallica tour in 1994, as Staley was too strung out. "Allison Chains lost tons and tons of money because they just couldn't be booked for tours."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Alice in Chains

facts.title: Give It Away Remix (1991) – Ministry's Al Jourgensen Used a Stoned Chicken on the Mixing Console
facts.body: Al Jourgensen was invited by the Red Hot Chili Peppers to produce a remix of "Give It Away" for their *Blood Sugar Sex Magik* album. His reported method: he brought a live chicken into the studio, blew marijuana smoke in its face until the bird was intoxicated, then let the stoned chicken stagger across the mixing desk. Wherever the chicken left a dropping, Jourgensen made an adjustment to the mix. "He brought a chicken into the studio and blew pot smoke in the chicken's face... Where the chicken pooped, Al made an adjustment to the mix."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Ministry

facts.title: "For Real" Self-Mutilation Incident (May 15, 1991)
facts.body: After a gig at the Norwich Art Center, NME reviewer Steve LeMack questioned the band's sincerity. During a private conversation, Richie Edwards dramatically carved the words "for real" into his forearm with a razor blade, resulting in 17 stitches and significant blood loss. A photographer captured the graphic event, leading to an internal debate at the NME offices about publishing the pictures, which were eventually printed and generated considerable notoriety for the band. "I mean, who carries a razor blade with him? And he carved the words for real into his forearm. Blood gushed everywhere, but Richie insisted on talking."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 9: The Disappearance of Richey Edwards
facts.name: Manic Street Preachers

facts.body: "Nevermind" was a pivotal album that exploded everything that had been building in indie and alternative music throughout the 1980s. It refined the sound pioneered by bands like Husker Dew and Sonic Youth, incorporating influences from Kiss, Black Sabbath, and The Beatles. It was one of the first alternative records to achieve success on both radio and MTV, establishing Nirvana as a bridge between the underground and mainstream rock scenes. "Everything that had been building through the 1980s, as far as indie and alternative and underground was concerned, exploded with this record."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Although "Smells Like Teen Spirit" became the album's unexpected hit single, the record label originally intended "Lithium" to be the first single. "Teen Spirit" was considered a "trial balloon" and was not expected to be a hit. "The real first single from Nevermind was going to be lithium."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Considered the most famous of the "Holy Trinity of Grunge" albums, its single was released on August 27, 1991, with the full album following on September 24, 1991. Within weeks, it was selling 300,000 copies a week and, by January, dethroned Michael Jackson's "Bad" from the number one spot on the Billboard charts, driving the rise of grunge and making alternative music mainstream. "Nirvana's never mind is the most famous of the Holy Trinity of Grunge albums."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Dave Grohl, who drummed for Nirvana, acknowledged that his drumming style on this classic album was influenced by and "ripped off" some of disco's best drummers. "Dave Girl said that he ripped off some of disco's best drummers when he played on the classic Nirvana album Never Mind."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Depending on the specific edition or pressing of the album "Nevermind" one possesses, a hidden track is likely present in the silence following the song "Something in the Way". This audio piece would roar into the listener's ears ten minutes after the preceding song concluded, often surprising millions who believed the album had finished. "It roars into your ears ten minutes after something in the way ends. And it scared the crap out of millions of people who thought they had let Nevermind run out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: During the filming of *Singles* in early 1991, Nirvana had not yet entered the studio to record their seminal album *Nevermind*. This highlights the period before the grunge explosion, showing that many key bands of the movement were still in their formative or pre-breakthrough stages. "Nirvana still hadn't gotten into the studio to record Nevermind."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: In a comparison to Slint's distinct sound and lack of resemblance to contemporary scenes, the transcript mentions that "hace años de esmana" (a garbled phrase, possibly meaning "some years ago" or "around that time") Nirvana released "Evermind" (likely a transcription error for *Nevermind*). This album's release saw Nirvana become the "abandonados" (abandoned ones, or potentially a transcription error for "abanderados" meaning standard-bearers/pioneers) of a new sound that would dominate the first half of the decade. "Hace años de esmana lanzaban a Evermind y fueron los abandonados de este nuevo sonido que dominaría la primera mitad de la década."
facts.source: Central Sonora
facts.episode: Spiderland: La Revolución del Rock Hecha por Adolescentes
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: In the fall of 1991, this album's sales were certified at an astounding 300,000 copies per week, a rate sustained for several months. The immense and unexpected success of Nevermind, highlighted by the new SoundScan system, prompted record labels to drastically shift their focus, initiating what became known as the "Grunge Gold Rush." "Nirvana's never-mind album was certified to selling 300,000 copies a week, every week, for months."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Nirvana's *Nevermind* is mentioned as an album that, like The Tragically Hip's *Fully Completely*, achieved diamond certification in Canada by selling over a million copies domestically. "Nirvana's Never Mind, Green Days, Ducky. Oh, and the hips up to here."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Nirvana's 1991 major label debut, *Nevermind*, was initially expected by Atlantic Records to sell only as well as the last Sonic Youth album. However, it achieved an astounding commercial success, ultimately selling 10 million copies and shattering all expectations, becoming a pivotal album in the grunge movement. "an oft repeated story about Nirvana was that their 1991 major label debut Nevermind was only expected to sell as well as the last Sonic Youth album, a benchmark that came to seem absurd when Nevermind sold 10 million copies."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: A Little Love and Some Tenderness Edition Part 1
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Nirvana's album "Never Mind" was released after they signed with DGC Records, a decision influenced by Sonic Youth's earlier signing with the same label. Kurt Cobain, a huge Sonic Youth fan, believed that if they could maintain creative control on a major label, Nirvana could too. "Nirvana signed, released Never Mind, Restless History."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Nirvana's second album and major label debut, produced by Butch Vig for DGC Records. Despite initial sales projections of 100,000 copies, it debuted at number 144 on the Billboard 200 and surged to number one after Christmas 1991, displacing Michael Jackson. The album, featuring a naked baby chasing a dollar bill on its cover, blended Seattle punk and metal with "enticing hooks" and a "pop sensibility." "The album with a naked baby on the cover, chasing a dollar bill on a fishing line, with song titles like Lithium, Territorial Pissings, and Stay Away was now the number one album in the country."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Released in 1991, "Nevermind" is considered one of the great albums of the 1990s. During its creation, Kurt Cobain expressed concerns about potential plagiarism, worrying that parts of "Smells Like Teen Spirit" resembled Boston's "More Than a Feeling" and that the quiet/loud structure mirrored The Pixies. The album's momentum was also potentially threatened by a copyright controversy surrounding the second single, "Come As You Are." "One of the great, great albums of the 1990s was Never Mind by Nirvana."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Released in the fall of 1991, this album built bridges and "resurrected rock and roll in the image of Generation X," marking a significant turning point where rock began to dominate pop music. "The bridges built by Nirvana's Nevermind album resurrected rock and roll in the image of Generation X."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Released on September 24, 1991, less than a month after Pearl Jam's "Ten," this album became the second part of the "Holy Trinity of Records" that launched grunge into the mainstream. Initial expectations were low, with only 46,251 copies manufactured and shipped. However, due to the overwhelming public reaction to its first single, the album sold out instantly and was moving 300,000 copies weekly within eight weeks, mobilizing a vast market of Generation X listeners. "Within eight weeks, this record was selling 300,000 copies every seven days."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: Released on September 24th, 1991, initial shipments totaled 46,251 copies, with industry expectations of only 50,000 sales if lucky. This album arrived during a stagnant period for rock music, dominated by classic rock, unamusing hair metal power ballads, and "crappy phony pop stars." It resonated deeply with Generation Xers who were seeking an emotional voice amidst recession and the Gulf War, providing them with music that spoke to their anger and fear. *Nevermind* swiftly became a monumental success, changing the entire rock landscape and shifting alternative music into the mainstream. "Never mind was one of those records that changed everything."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.body: The album included "Smells Like Teen Spirit," which was one of the songs written specifically for it, long after most other tracks had been demoed. This later songwriting process is why few studio bootlegs exist for this particular track, unlike much of the rest of the album. "Teen Spirit was one of the songs for Nevermind written long after the tracks were originally demoed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: The album's release on September 24, 1991, drastically altered the musical landscape, marking a pivotal moment in the speaker's musical life. It shared its release date with *Blood Sugar Sex Magik* by the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Warner (GDGC's) initially projected sales of 50,000 to 100,000 copies, but the album quickly soared to 300,000 copies per week. In January, it famously dislodged Michael Jackson from the number one spot on the Billboard album charts. "I remember September 25, 1991 walking into Medeville High School and my entire musical landscape changed because of what happened the day before with the drop of Nevermind."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.body: This album became "the biggest thing in the world" after its release. In the spring of 1992, following its massive success, Kurt Cobain sought to rewrite the band's royalty arrangements, demanding 90% of songwriting royalties, backdated to the album's September 1991 release. After heated arguments, Kurt was eventually "bargained down to 75%." "In the spring of 1992, after the Never Mind album had become the biggest thing in the world, Kurt Cobain decided he wanted to rewrite the band's royalty arrangements."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

facts.body: This album became immensely popular, but Kurt Cobain felt it was "too slick and wasn't punk rock enough." The follow-up, *In Utero*, was intentionally made to contrast with its polished sound. "Kurt also didn't like the record company game very much. He thought that never mind was too slick and wasn't punk rock enough."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: This album features the polished, official version of "Smells Like Teen Spirit," which, in its earliest demo stages, was "almost a minute longer" and had different words and arrangements. "But that's how the song sounded during its earliest days. The words are different. The arrangement is different, and it's almost a minute longer than what we got on, never mind."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nevermind

facts.body: This album had a "sharp sheen" applied to it by mastering engineer Andy Wallace, who extended the high frequencies of the two-track mix provided by the band and producer Butch Vig. This mastering technique helped the songs achieve greater clarity and cut-through, especially when compared to the original studio mix, which sounded muffled and dull. "Andy Wallace applied the sharp sheen to Nirvana's Nevermind album."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

"That album was never mind and we don't need to go into that story again."

facts.body: This album, produced by Butch Vig, was released on September 24, 1991, with an initial distribution of 46,251 copies to record stores. The band initially hoped to sell around 200,000 copies, but "Nevermind" became an unprecedented success, selling 300,000 copies a week by Christmas. It sold its first million copies in just 65 days and doubled that figure in another 41 days, ultimately staying on the Billboard charts for 92 uninterrupted weeks and generating over $100 million in gross revenues. "Released to radio on August 27th, 1991, and on album to everyone on September the 24th, 1991, smells like teen spirits. The album of course was never mind."

facts.title: Cultural Impact
facts.body: "Nevermind" was a pivotal album that exploded everything that had been building in indie and alternative music throughout the 1980s. It refined the sound pioneered by bands like Husker Dew and Sonic Youth, incorporating influences from Kiss, Black Sabbath, and The Beatles. It was one of the first alternative records to achieve success on both radio and MTV, establishing Nirvana as a bridge between the underground and mainstream rock scenes. "Everything that had been building through the 1980s, as far as indie and alternative and underground was concerned, exploded with this record."
